title: What If You Spent the Winter at the South Pole?

scenes.text: What if you spent the winter at the South Pole? After February, no plane can reach you.
The last flight leaves in mid-February. The next lands in early November, almost eight months later.
Winter highs are around minus 59 degrees Celsius. Lows reach minus 75, and the record is minus 82.
Jet fuel can gel in that cold, so winter flights are considered too dangerous.
Only about 40 to 50 people stay, the same group all winter, with no fresh food or supplies arriving.
The Sun sets in March and doesn't return for about six months. Winter there is a long night.

description:
What if you spent the winter at the South Pole?
For almost eight months no plane can land, and temperatures fall below minus 70 degrees Celsius.
